implementation_summary: Created the S1 skeleton for the 3-party property spec at e2e/tests/multi-user-3p.property.spec.ts. Contains exactly ONE test ('[C0,S5,S6,S7,S10] settled-state equality holds across A/B/C') under ONE test.describe.serial ('[C0,S5,S6,S7,S10,A7-A12,A14] 3-party multi-user property'). beforeAll opens three BrowserContext + three Page (A/B/C), authenticates each against its bunker, and caches cachedPubkeyA/B/C at module scope; afterAll closes all three contexts. ModelState3P models a single shared group (groupId/groupName), three distinct per-actor pubkeys (pubkeyA/B/C), per-actor membership flags (memberA/B/C), a group-scoped tasks Map, per-actor epochSequenceA/B/C arrays, lastSwitched, plus helpers pubkey()/actorIsMember()/recordEpoch()/reset(). RealSystem3P holds pageA/B/C with page() accessor and implements the stable readers getTasks/getTask/quiesce that S2-S5 rely on. Commands and headline assertions are intentionally deferred to S2-S5; the placeholder test body asserts the skeleton wiring (three distinct cached pubkeys, model.pubkey()/real.page() accessors). All five S1 ACs satisfied: file exists (FILE-1); one test under one serial describe verified via `playwright test --list` (FILE-2); title contains [C0,S5,S6,S7,S10] (FILE-3); three contexts/pages created+torn down with per-bunker auth (FILE-4); cachedPubkeyA/B/C read once post-auth at module scope (FILE-5).

bunker_setup_decision.choice: STATIC per-identity constants — E2E_BUNKER_URL (auth-helper.ts), E2E_BUNKER_B_URL (auth-helper-b.ts), E2E_BUNKER_C_URL (auth-helper-c.ts).
bunker_setup_decision.rationale: Honors the spec default (Design Decision #8 + AC-3P-FILE-4 name the static constants as the literal requirement; architecture.md constraint #2 sets static-constants as the default and spawnSpecBunker x3 as an explicit S7 amendment, not an S1 default). Actor C is authenticated via two-party.ts authenticate(pageC, E2E_BUNKER_C_URL) — NOT the bare authenticateAsBunkerC — so C gets clearAppState + slot-pin + __notestrTestPubkey hook-wait parity with A and B (architecture.md constraint #3).
bunker_setup_decision.risk_flagged_for_S7: KeyPackage accumulation on the SHARED A/B/C bunker identities. The 2-party and multi-user-md PROPERTY specs deliberately use spawnSpecBunker per-spec fresh bunkers precisely to avoid KP buildup across the ~15-iteration command loop. The S1 skeleton runs no command loop and never invites, so it adds at most one NIP-33-replaceable KP per identity (identical load to the already-green three-party.spec.ts, which uses these same static constants). The accumulation only materializes once S5 wires the full command loop. If S7 wall-clock validation shows KP-accumulation flakiness, the known mitigation is spawnSpecBunker x3, which would be an EXPLICIT amendment to AC-3P-FILE-4 rather than a silent deviation.
bunker_setup_decision.alternative_considered: spawnSpecBunker('mu-3p-A'/'-B'/'-C') x3 (the 2-party property convention). Deferred to S7 per the architecture's stated posture; not adopted in S1 to avoid silently deviating from a frozen AC.

codex.p2_finding: Avoid publishing property-test key packages to shared A/B/C bunkers (multi-user-3p.property.spec.ts:260-277) — shared-bunker auth accumulates stale KPs and can make later specs flakier; recommends per-spec bunkers.
codex.disposition: NOT actioned in S1 (deliberate). This is the exact KP-accumulation tension the exploration + architecture pre-named; the spec default (AC-3P-FILE-4 static constants) is honored in S1 and the risk is flagged for S7 wall-clock validation. Recorded as post-impl verification question VQ-S1-011 so the verifier sees the judgment call. Codex itself noted 'the skeleton itself never exercises invites'.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: The mandatory review's working-tree scope only diffs TRACKED changes, so the first Ollama pass reviewed only BACKLOG.json/package-lock.json and silently missed the entire new untracked spec file — a clean 'approve' that had not actually seen the implementation. I had to `git add -N` the new file to force it into the diff and re-run. Any agent creating a brand-new file and then running these reviews must stage it (intent-to-add) first, or the review is a false pass.
